title: Intertwining Sets For Cover Representations
body_html:
Intertwining Sets For Cover Representations

Let $H,H'\subset G$ be closed subgroups. For ordinary representations $\sigma_0$ of $H$ and $\sigma'_0$ of $H'$, define

$$ I(\sigma_0,\sigma'_0) = \{g\in G: \operatorname{Hom}_{H^g\cap H'}(\sigma_0^g,\sigma'_0)\ne 0\}. $$

For $\alpha$-genuine representations $\sigma$ of $\widetilde H$ and $\sigma'$ of $\widetilde H'$, define

$$ I(\sigma,\sigma') = \{\widetilde g\in\widetilde G: \operatorname{Hom}_{\widetilde H^{\widetilde g}\cap\widetilde H'} (\sigma^{\widetilde g},\sigma')\ne 0\}. $$

If $H$ and $H'$ are prime-to-$Z$ compact subgroups, so the relevant splittings are unique, the draft asserts

$$ I(\sigma,\sigma') = \widetilde{I(\sigma_0,\sigma'_0)}. $$

Here $\sigma_0=\sigma|_H$ and $\sigma'_0=\sigma'|_{H'}$ under the unique splittings.

Draft Caution

The TeX has a typo in the label spelling, interwining. The mathematical statement is used to transfer intertwining questions from a tame cover back to the underlying group.
